catalog_quote: II Initial main stress, no info on sec stress: ... Nhuwala (T74): Inferred from: O'Grady, Geoffrey N. (1958). Fieldnotes. Ms, AIATSIS, Canberra. [p. 242] ... [Appendix D preamble, p. 235] This is a list of languages categorised by stress type and annotated with the main descriptive source and some codes denoting special characteristics of the stress pattern in that language. ... Some of the entries have no descriptive source. These must be handled with caution. The stress pattern in these languages was deduced from old scanty material found in the Australian Institute for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies (AIATSIS) library and at the Australian National University (ANU). It may be that some of them have been mistakenly placed in a certain category, due to missing crucial information. Yet, they were included for completeness sake.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress on the first syllable of the word; nothing known about secondary stress. This is Goedemans's own inference from O'Grady's 1958 unpublished fieldnotes (a wordlist-level manuscript), not a published description; no Nhuwala forms are given.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None reported ('no info on sec stress').
new_statements.exceptions: None; the survey preamble warns that inferred entries may be mistakenly categorised.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, presumably citation forms from a wordlist; no phrase-level information. No first-hand phonological description of Nhuwala exists (Thieberger 1993: no grammar, sketch, texts or intensive fieldwork).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottocode nhuw1239 = Nhuwala (also Noala, Nuala, Ngoala, Nooela, Nuela; Tindale T74; AIATSIS/AUSTLANG code W30, not W22). Dormant/extinct since the late 1990s; Onslow/Ashburton-mouth coast, Pilbara WA. Goedemans's entry is labelled 'Nhuwala (T74)', i.e. the same variety. No dialect information exists (Thieberger 1993 §4.4.9).

sources.citation: Dench, Alan C. 1995. Martuthunira: A language of the Pilbara region of Western Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-125.
sources.note: Mentions Nhuwala only in the territory/classification discussion (68% cognacy with Martuthunira; 'not yet enough data to enable confident classification'); its phonology chapter is Martuthunira only, nothing on Nhuwala stress.

sources.citation: Thieberger, Nicholas. 1993. Handbook of Western Australian Aboriginal languages south of the Kimberley region. Pacific Linguistics C-124. §4.4.9 Nhuwala, pp. 126-127.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Records that no one worked intensively on the language, 'Grammar or sketch grammar: None', 'Practical spelling system: None'; only word lists: Brandenstein (1969g diaries), O'Grady (1957-58 'Materials on the suffixing languages of Western Australia', MS), Paterson (1957 lexical test lists); Bates n.d. pronoun outline; Dench 1982a Jurruru fieldnotes with one Nhuwala sentence. AIATSIS code W30.
